summary: Iteration 2 verified the CMS refactor: fixtures feature fully removed, editable content system for home/story/membership/contact/sponsors is live end-to-end. 29/29 backend pytest cases pass, all frontend flows pass. Highlights: GET /api/content returns all 5 keys, GET /api/content/{key} works per-section, /api/admin/content/{key} enforces admin (401 anon / 403 member / 200 admin), /api/sponsors reads items from site_content, /api/admin/stats now returns revenue/tickets_sold/members/active_members/shows_total/campaigns (no fixtures/no upcoming_shows), /api/admin/fixtures returns 404. Frontend: admin sidebar shows Overview/Shows/Members/Ticket Sales/Bulk Email/Edit Pages with NO Lighting Assets; Dashboard shows 4 stat cards + Community panel (no fixtures text); AdminPages has 5 tabs (pagetab-home/story/membership/contact/sponsors); editing Membership 'title' via field-title + save-page-btn is immediately reflected on public /membership; Home tab lists 4 hero-slide img-rows; Sponsors tab lists 4 obj-rows; public Home shows 4 hero-dots slideshow; Our Story, Contact, Sponsors render seeded content; member->admin redirects to /portal; anon->/portal redirects to /login; Stripe checkout returns a checkout.stripe.com URL. Original CMS content was restored after edit.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~750 lines and still growing (added CMS routes). Splitting into routers (auth, shows, payments, admin, content) would help maintainability.

Dual auth surface (cookie access_token + Authorization Bearer) is intentional but /auth/logout only clears the cookie; frontend uses localStorage 'pp_token' and clears client-side. Consider consolidating on one strategy and documenting.

PUT /api/admin/content/{key} accepts any dict as body.data with no schema validation per key. This is by design (flexible CMS) but a member/admin typo could break a public page silently. Consider a light-weight per-key schema (or shape check) plus a 'reset to default' admin endpoint.
site_content is upserted on PUT but there is no history/versioning; a bad edit cannot be rolled back except by admin re-edit. Consider retaining previous data snapshot on write.
seed_data_creation: Backend auto-seeds admin, demo member, 4 shows (all normalised to status=past by migration), and DEFAULT_CONTENT for the 5 CMS keys. Tests created and cleaned up TEST_ prefixed shows/campaigns; the roundtrip CMS test restored the original membership content in a finally block.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (pytest, 29 cases). To run: `pytest /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py -v`. Old iteration_1 fixtures-CRUD tests were removed and replaced with TestFixturesRemoved (expects 404) and TestContent (CMS CRUD + authz + roundtrip). Frontend uses Authorization: Bearer with localStorage 'pp_token'. Admin nav data-testids: admin-nav-overview/shows/members/ticket-sales/bulk-email/edit-pages. AdminPages testids: admin-pages, pagetab-<key>, field-<key>, img-row-<i>, obj-row-<i>, save-page-btn. Home slideshow: hero-dot-<i>. All 4 seeded shows are status=past by design (no Book button, only 'Season closed' + Details).
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Feature removal and CMS addition are fully wired backend↔frontend.
